findings.issue_text: [BUG] The embed stylesheet is referenced via stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' but 'embed' is never added to config.assets.precompile, so Sprockets raises AssetNotFound in production where config.assets.compile is false. Every request to /embed/best returns a 500 in production instead of rendering the embed page, because non-application assets are not precompiled by default and the diff adds no precompile entry for embed.css.

[BUG] poll_feed calls i.content.scrub, which raises NoMethodError both when the feed item has no content element (i.content is nil) and on any Ruby runtime without String#scrub (Ruby < 2.1, which this codebase era supports). Any RSS/Atom feed whose items lack a content element (common for RSS 2.0 feeds with only descriptions) crashes the scheduled job with NoMethodError on nil.scrub, and since retry is disabled the poll silently never imports that feed; on Ruby 1.9/2.0 the job fails on every item unconditionally.

[BUG] The best view calls post.user.small_avatar_url and post.user.username without any nil check, so a post whose author was deleted crashes the template. An embed page for a topic containing a post from a deleted user raises NoMethodError on nil.small_avatar_url, returning a 500 inside the customer's iframe instead of the discussion listing.

[ADVISORY] The new ruby-readability and simple-rss gems are added to the Gemfile but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated in this diff, leaving the primary Gemfile.lock stale. Anyone running plain `bundle install` (CI, deploy images built from the main lockfile) gets an out-of-sync lockfile error, and a `bundle install --deployment` deploy fails outright until the lockfile is regenerated.

[ADVISORY] An already-shipped migration is edited to add force: true, so re-running it (db:migrate:redo, db:reset on staging, or a rollback+re-up) drops the existing top_topics table and all its ranking data instead of failing safely. Operators who redo or replay this migration on an environment with populated top_topics data silently lose it, and the change is invisible to databases that already applied the original version.

[ADVISORY] retrieve_topic.rb requires 'email/sender' which this job never uses, and both require_dependency lines assume lib/topic_retriever.rb is on the autoload path without any autoload-eager test coverage for that assumption in this job. The unused require pulls the mail-sending stack into every retrieve_topic worker for no reason; the next refactor of app/lib file layout breaks this job at load time rather than test time.

[BUG] The header block terminates with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to a bare `end if` in the generated Ruby and is a syntax error, so the best view raises on every render. Every successful embed request with an existing topic_id crashes with an ActionView::Template::Error (500) instead of rendering the comment list; the controller specs never render the view because TopicView is mocked, so nothing catches it.

[BUG] The RSS/Atom path stores feed content as raw HTML (cook_method :raw_html, `post.cooked == post.raw`) with no sanitization step, while the ruby-readability path in import_remote only whitelists a few tags/attributes — the PollFeed path bypasses even that. Any `<script>` or `onerror=` attribute in a feed item's content is stored verbatim and rendered via `raw post.cooked` on the embed page and the forum topic, giving a feed author stored XSS on the Discourse instance; the topic_embed_spec only asserts cooked == raw, never that dangerous tags are stripped.

[BUG] `request.referer` is interpolated unescaped into the inline JavaScript string, so a referer whose path contains a single quote breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary JS on the forum origin. An attacker who can make a victim's browser send a referer like `http://<embeddable_host>/');alert(1);//` (host matches so ensure_embeddable passes, path is unconstrained) gets script execution in the embed page under the forum's origin.

[BUG] `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError for any RSS 2.0 item that has no content element (SimpleRSS exposes tags via method_missing and RSS 2.0 items carry `description`, not `content`). The hourly poll job crashes on the first item lacking content, so no feed items are ever imported and every subsequent hourly run dies at the same item; the poll_feed_spec only stubs the setting guards and never exercises poll_feed itself, so the gap is untested.

[ADVISORY] The loading view unconditionally reloads the iframe every 30 seconds forever, with no attempt count and no terminal state. When retrieval legitimately cannot succeed (retrieve_topic is throttled by embed_by_username being unset, readability finds no content, or the fetch fails), the embedding site burns bandwidth with an infinite reload loop and visitors see 'Loading Discussion...' permanently.

[ADVISORY] import_remote is a new non-trivial network-facing code path (readability fetch + title fallback + import) with zero test coverage in the diff, and import's title handling accepts nil titles because PostCreator is called with skip_validations. A feed item or retrieved page with a blank title creates a topic whose title is nil; topic.url and the embed header links then break, and a regression in import_remote's fetch/fallback logic would ship unnoticed since no spec touches it.

[ADVISORY] The embed script calls appendChild on `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` without a null check, and no test in the diff covers the JS. A site operator who pastes the script without the matching `<div id='discourse-comments'>` element gets a TypeError that silently kills the whole IIFE, including the resize postMessage listener, so embedded comments never appear and there is no error surfaced.

[ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs/srcs starting with a single `/`, so protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/img.png`) and relative paths without a leading slash fall through unchanged. Protocol-relative URLs get mangled into `http://<host>//cdn...` broken links in imported posts; feed authors whose sites use protocol-relative assets see broken images/links in every embedded copy of the article.

[ADVISORY] The Disqus importer is rewritten to route through TopicEmbed.import_remote, which is unrelated to the stated intent of 'embed URL handling and validation' and silently drops the --category option and the original created_at handling. Anyone re-running the documented disqus import task loses the ability to target a category and imported topics get current timestamps instead of the Disqus thread's original date; this refactor is not traceable to any requirement in the PR description.

[BUG] This diff adds `force: true` to the pre-existing create_top_topics migration, an unrelated and destructive change to a migration that already shipped. Any environment that re-runs migrations (db:migrate:redo, bootstrap, or a partially-migrated install where this migration has not yet run against existing data) silently DROPs the existing top_topics table and its data; nothing in the PR's stated intent requires touching this migration.

[ADVISORY] A new client-side admin settings category 'embedding' is added to the locale file but no client code, settings pane, or route in this diff consumes it, so the three new site settings (embeddable_host, feed_polling_enabled, etc.) have no UI anywhere. Operators must edit the database or rails console to configure embedding; the locale key is dead weight until a matching admin UI lands in a future PR, indicating the feature ships half-scoped.

[ADVISORY] Whitespace-only reformatting of the unrelated migrate_word_counts migration (trailing space removal and newline-at-EOF change) is included in this PR. The diff contains noise in a file unrelated to embedding, making review and blame history harder for future changes to that migration; purely formatting churn with no requirement behind it.

[ADVISORY] The PollFeed specs only test the three site-setting gates; the actual poll_feed body (feed_key, item URL fallback to i.id, CGI.unescapeHTML scrub, TopicEmbed.import invocation) added in this diff has zero test coverage. A regression in the feed-parsing logic (e.g., a feed whose items only carry an atom id, or content with escaped HTML) will pass the entire suite while silently creating no topics or malformed ones; the only new non-trivial parsing logic in the PR is untested.

[ADVISORY] TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire hourly-scheduled Jobs::PollFeed job inline on the embed request path, coupling the retriever to the scheduled job rather than a shared extraction. A site with feed polling enabled pays a full feed download/parse inside the RetrieveTopic background job triggered by every unknown embed_url, and any exception raised by SimpleRSS.parse/open aborts the subsequent fetch_http fallback, so HTTP scraping never happens for feed-enabled sites when the feed is broken.

[BUG] poll_feed calls i.content unconditionally, which is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds (SimpleRSS exposes 'description' for RSS items; 'content' only exists on Atom entries), so the hourly poll raises NoMethodError on nil.scrub and no items are ever imported. Any site configuring a plain RSS feed (the common case for the feed_polling_url setting) gets zero imports — the job dies partway through the first item every hour, and sidekiq_options retry: false means it never retries or reports; the admin sees a silently dead feature.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously in-process, fetching and importing the ENTIRE feed just to serve one embed_url. A single visitor hitting /embed/best for a not-yet-imported URL triggers a full-feed HTTP fetch plus a full-feed import pass (one PostCreator per new item, with rate limits and notifications) inside a Sidekiq worker; a large feed turns each embed request into unbounded work and multiplies load on the embeddable site and the forum, where the intended design was 'retrieve one article'.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import does a check-then-act (where(embed_url:).first then create!) with no rescue on the unique index, and the controller path can enqueue duplicate RetrieveTopic jobs concurrently. Two visitors loading the same new embed URL within the same window race past the existence check; the loser's create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique inside the transaction, failing the job with an unhandled error — the retry semantics then re-fetch the remote article for a URL that already exists.

[ADVISORY] The change-detection and revision path only covers post raw content: content_sha1 is computed from contents and PostRevisor.revise! is given only new_raw, so a feed item whose title changed is never updated. When an RSS/Atom article's headline is corrected after import, the Discourse topic keeps the stale title forever even though the poller runs hourly and re-imports the item — embed viewers see the wrong discussion title with no operator path to fix it short of manual edits.

[ADVISORY] The raw_html cook_method returns raw completely outside the cooking pipeline — it bypasses both the Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook) hook and any sanitization that the normal cook path performs. Every plugin hooking after_post_cook (polls, oneboxes, math, etc.) silently no-ops for imported posts, and arbitrary HTML fetched from an external feed (attacker-controllable content in the feed) is stored verbatim as post.cooked and rendered with `raw` in the embed view — a stored-XSS ingestion path that the normal pipeline exists to prevent.

[ADVISORY] feed_key is defined (a SHA1 cache key for the feed's modified state) but never used anywhere — the poller re-downloads and re-parses the full feed unconditionally every hour. Dead code that documents an intent (conditional fetch / change detection) the implementation dropped; the next maintainer assumes feed modifications are checked and bandwidth is saved, when in fact every hour incurs a full fetch and full-iteration import regardless of feed changes.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten Disqus import drops both the created_at option (posts previously got Date.parse(t[:created_at])) and the category option, and now routes through TopicEmbed.import_remote which sets cook_method raw_html. Anyone re-running the disqus import after this change gets topics dated 'now' instead of their original thread dates (destroying chronological ordering of imported discussions) and can no longer target a category, plus imported content is now unsanitized raw HTML; the old CLI contract (--category flag) silently disappears.

[ADVISORY] poll_feed calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no size limit, and import_remote calls open(url).read the same way, materializing the whole document in memory. A misconfigured or hostile feed_polling_url (or embeddable-host page, since embed URLs are attacker-supplied via the embed_url param and only host-checked) serving a multi-gigabyte response is read fully into the Sidekiq worker's memory, exhausting worker RAM for all tenants of that process.

[BUG] cook returns raw HTML unfiltered, bypassing the entire Markdown/sanitization pipeline including Plugin::Filter(:after_post_cook) for raw_html posts. RSS feed items and readability-extracted remote HTML fetched via feed_polling_url or import_remote are stored and served verbatim with raw post.cooked in embed/best and the main topic renderer, so a feed author or compromised embedded site injects arbitrary <script> into the Discourse origin — cookie/session theft on every visitor of the embedding host and the forum itself.

[BUG] This diff adds force: true to create_table :top_topics on an already-shipped migration, so any environment that already ran the original version re-runs it and force-drops the existing top_topics table. Deploying this on a live site that has already executed the 20131223171005 migration destroys all top_topics rows (hot/daily/weekly/monthly top rankings) with no recovery path.

[BUG] create_table :topic_embeds, force: true drops any pre-existing topic_embeds table instead of failing loudly. If topic_embeds was created out-of-band or by a prior deploy branch, running db:migrate silently discards all embed-to-topic mappings, orphaning imported topics and causing embed/best to re-import duplicate topics.

[BUG] i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError when the feed item has no content element (common in Atom feeds where only summary is present). The hourly PollFeed job crashes on the first content-less item, retries are disabled (sidekiq_options retry: false), and every subsequent feed item is silently never imported — feed polling stops working with no operator-visible error beyond sidekiq dead-set noise.

[BUG] The Disqus import rewrite silently changes accepted behavior: it drops the --category/-c option, discards the original thread created_at (posts now get import time instead of Date.parse(t[:created_at])), and no longer posts the [Permalink] raw — instead it fetches each thread over HTTP through readability. Operators running the documented disqus import after this change get topics in the default category with wrong timestamps and import failures whenever t[:link] is unreachable (TopicEmbed.import_remote does open(url)), breaking the previously-working offline import path with no deprecation notice.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import mutates the caller's contents string with << and interpolates the raw URL into an HTML attribute, then wraps it in content_sha1, so the same RSS content with a URL containing a quote would both break the imported_from link markup and change the hash on every poll. Feed items whose link contains characters needing HTML escaping produce malformed imported posts; downstream, feed polls see a stable sha so updates stop being detected.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside the RetrieveTopic background job rather than enqueuing it, performing a blocking HTTP fetch of the entire feed inside the retrieve path. Every embed miss from a non-staff visitor on a site with feed_polling_enabled triggers a full synchronous feed parse + per-item TopicEmbed.import inside a Sidekiq worker, making embed first-views arbitrarily slow and allowing the embeddable host's feed latency to consume worker capacity.

[BUG] When topic_id is found, TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) raises for a deleted/trashed topic and the view template dereferences @topic_view.topic.url on line 2 of best.html.erb without any posts-present guard on the header, so the loading-view branch's nil-safety is asymmetric with the found branch. A visitor embedding a URL whose topic was later deleted gets a 500 from /embed/best instead of a graceful fallback or the loading view.

[ADVISORY] The resize postMessage is sent to '<%= request.referer %>' as a literal targetOrigin while the receiving embed.js checks discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 with a leading-string prefix match. Any origin whose domain begins with the Discourse URL string (e.g. discourseUrl.example.attacker.com when discourseUrl is 'discourseUrl') passes the client check, and the iframe resizes on spoofed messages; combined with the raw-HTML rendering this is a second injection surface for the embedding page.

[BUG] PollFeed imports unescaped RSS/Atom item content as a raw_html post with no HTML sanitization, which is then rendered verbatim. Unlike TopicEmbed.import_remote (which filters through Readability's tag/attribute whitelist), the poll_feed path calls TopicEmbed.import directly with CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) — so a malicious or compromised feed served at the admin-configured feed_polling_url injects arbitrary HTML (

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import string-interpolates the URL into an HTML attribute without escaping, so a URL containing a single quote breaks out of the href attribute. A URL like http://embeddablehost/x' onmouseover='alert(1) passes the /^https?:\/\// regex check and embeddable_host match (host is unaffected by path characters) but injects arbitrary attributes/HTML into the 'imported_from' footer, which is stored as a raw_html post and rendered with `raw post.cooked`. An attacker who controls a page URL (e.g. a comment URL harvested by the RSS feed, or an embed_url path on the embeddable host) achieves stored XSS against all forum users.

[ADVISORY] The embeddable-host gate is enforced by the client-controlled Referer header, making it trivially bypassable trust-the-client authorization. Anyone can curl /embed/best with a spoofed Referer matching embeddable_host and enumerate/render any topic's content via the TopicView branch (topic_id_for_embed performs no referer-independent scoping). The actual SSRF protection of the retriever does not depend on this check, so impact is limited to unauthorized content disclosure/crawling of a forum intended to be restricted to embedding on one host — but the gate provides no real boundary.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of strict origin equality. Any origin whose string representation appears anywhere in discourseUrl passes the check; because origins are full scheme+host strings this is hard to exploit with the current constant, but it is a fragile pattern that silently breaks if discourseUrl ever contains a user-influenced component or redirects are followed. A future maintainer copying this pattern into a handler that mutates the DOM beyond iframe.height gets script injection on the embedding page.

[ADVISORY] request.referer is echoed directly into an inline <script> as a JS string literal. The Referer header is attacker-controlled and includes arbitrary path/query data; ERB's HTML escaping of quotes (to ') prevents JS execution but produces a malformed string / syntax error when the referer contains a single quote, breaking the resize postMessage for those embeds. Any string header interpolated into a script context should be JSON-encoded, not HTML-escaped.

[ADVISORY] open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) uses Kernel#open on a configuration value, which executes shell commands when the value begins with a pipe character. Ruby's open() treats a string starting with '|' as a command to run, so any actor able to set site settings (or compromise the settings store) gets arbitrary command execution on the app server rather than just an HTTP fetch. Per the config-as-attacker-input threat model, config-backed sinks into open() should be treated as command-injection-capable; use open-uri's URI(...) or Net::HTTP instead.

[ADVISORY] import_remote calls open(url) with the user-supplied embed_url, and open() invokes command execution for pipe-prefixed strings. The invalid_host? check (URI(@embed_url).host == embeddable_host) rejects pipe-prefixed strings since URI() raises, so this path is currently contained; but the safety depends on TopicRetriever always running before import_remote — the Disqus thor task calls import_remote directly with t[:link] from a local file, so any future caller that skips the retriever check gets command execution from unvalidated input. The command-injection primitive (Kernel#open on untrusted URLs) should be removed, not merely gated upstream.

[BUG] The test named "is 404 without an embed_url" asserts only response.should_not be_success, and the params.require branch is never reached because ensure_embeddable raises first when embeddable_host is unset. The test passes whether the controller returns a 404, a 403, or a 500, and the params.require(:embed_url) path has zero test coverage — a regression that breaks the missing-param contract (e.g., raising a 500 instead of 400) would go undetected because the error thrown by the before_filter masks it.

[ADVISORY] The 'tells the topic retriever to work' test verifies only that a TopicRetriever mock's retrieve method is called, never that Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) receives the correct embed_url and user_id payload that the controller actually constructs. The argument-passing from controller to job to retriever (embed_url string, user_id for current_user) is unverified; if Jobs.enqueue is a no-op in test mode the expectation goes unfulfilled or the inline path silently skips user_id, and a regression dropping or mangling the embed_url in the enqueue payload would not be caught.

[ADVISORY] The 'creates a topic view' test fully mocks TopicView.new, so the best.html.erb view — including the new @topic_view.posts.present? branches and raw post.cooked rendering — is never rendered or asserted. Any breakage in the new embed view template (nil post.user, wrong posts collection from the best:5 option) passes the controller spec; only the mocked constructor call is verified, testing the mock rather than the rendered behavior the diff adds.

[ADVISORY] Every test in poll_feed_spec only exercises the settings gate in execute (poll_feed never/once) — the actual poll_feed method (SimpleRSS parsing, the url-blank/non-http fallback to i.id, CGI.unescapeHTML with scrub, delegation to TopicEmbed.import) has zero assertions anywhere in the diff. The feed-import logic — including the branch where i.link is blank or non-http and falls back to i.id — can regress entirely while all four specs stay green; an operator enabling feed polling gets untested code parsing arbitrary remote feeds.

[ADVISORY] All 'valid host' tests stub retrieved_recently?, so the real Redis throttle (setnx + 60s expire in retrieved_recent?), perform_retrieve's early return on existing TopicEmbed, the PollFeed delegation, and fetch_http are never executed by any test. A bug in the Redis throttle logic (e.g., key never set, or expire missing so throttling becomes permanent) or in perform_retrieve's exist-check ordering passes the suite untouched; only the boolean gate dispatch is covered.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls is only tested with a default-port http URL; the non-standard-port branch (prefix << ":#{uri.port}") and TopicEmbed.import_remote (ruby-readability document parsing, tags/attributes whitelist, opts[:title] fallback) have no test in the diff. The port-appending branch can produce malformed URLs (double slashes, wrong scheme) without detection, and import_remote — the path used by the Disqus thor task and the retrieve_topic job — can break (Readability API change, open(url) failure) with the entire spec suite green.

[ADVISORY] Jobs::RetrieveTopic has no spec anywhere in the diff (checked spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb — none reference RetrieveTopic), so the user lookup, the raise on missing embed_url, and the no_throttle: user.try(:staff?) option are untested. A regression in the job (e.g., enqueuing with a stale user_id causing user to be nil and throttling staff incorrectly, or the InvalidParameters raise firing on every call) surfaces only in production sidekiq, not in CI.

[BUG] An already-shipped migration was retroactively modified to add force: true, making it destructive on re-run. Running db:migrate:redo or db:rollback past this version on a production database executes DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics and silently destroys all top_topics rows (daily/weekly/monthly score aggregates) with no backup/export step; the data is unrecoverable without recomputation, and the change ships in a PR whose feature (topic embeds) has nothing to do with top_topics.

[ADVISORY] The new topic_embeds migration uses force: true on a table that, once shipped and populated, will be dropped and its data lost if the migration is ever re-run (redo, or a fresh db:migrate against an environment where the table pre-exists from a prior deploy). After this migration ships and TopicEmbed rows accumulate, any db:migrate:redo or rollback+re-run wipes every topic_embed mapping; embedded sites then re-import articles as duplicate topics because embed_url lookups find nothing, silently forking comment threads off existing posts.

[ADVISORY] topic_id and post_id are created null: false with no foreign key constraints and no indexes, while TopicEmbed#import updates the associated post on every content change and embed_controller reads topic_id from this table. Deleting a topic or post (standard Discourse behavior, e.g. after post destroy jobs) leaves orphaned topic_embeds rows; TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed then returns a topic_id for a nonexistent topic and EmbedController#best constructs TopicView.new with a deleted topic id, erroring on the embed endpoint — and without an index on topic_id, the periodic import re-lookups degrade. Orphan cleanup has to be handled out-of-band forever because the migration never establishes referential integrity.

[BUG] The update path revises the embed's post but writes only the new raw via PostRevisor with skip_validations, and if post is nil (the embed row exists but its post_id points at a deleted post, allowed by the missing FK above), PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises and the PollFeed job dies, blocking all subsequent feed items from importing. A single stale topic_embed row (topic/post deleted by a moderator while the RSS feed still lists the article) makes the hourly PollFeed job raise before reaching remaining feed items — with retry: false set on the job, every poll after that silently fails and the feed stops importing until the orphan row is manually removed.

[ADVISORY] The new NOT NULL cook_method column relies on its integer default to backfill every existing post, coupling the existing-row semantics to the Post.cook_methods Enum ordering rather than a named constant or comment, with no migration-side assertion of what 1 means. Future maintainers reordering or inserting values into Post.cook_methods (e.g. adding a :markdown method first) silently reclassify the backfilled rows: all existing posts render through the wrong cook pipeline after a code change with no migration accompanying it. The value is correct today (1 = :regular) but the coupling is undocumented at the migration site.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import returns nil silently when PostCreator.create fails, and the RetrieveTopic job then completes 'successfully' with no topic created, so the embed iframe loops on the loading page forever. The embed controller renders 'loading' and reloads every 30s (loading.html.erb); if the article fetch fails or the post is rejected (e.g., empty title/content after readability extraction), the job enqueued from EmbedController#best completes with no error, no embed row is created, and the visitor's browser reloads /embed/best in an infinite loop with no error ever surfaced to the user or the logs.

[BUG] A single bad feed item aborts the whole items loop with an unhandled NoMethodError (i.content or i.title nil for a valid Atom entry), and with sidekiq_options retry: false the remaining items are permanently dropped with no retry. The first item missing content raises NoMethodError on i.content.scrub; every subsequent item in the feed is skipped, and because retry is disabled there is no later attempt — feed items are silently missing from the forum with no log identifying which item broke the run.

[BUG] On the update path, embed.post is dereferenced without a nil check, so an embed row whose post was deleted crashes with NoMethodError inside the scheduled PollFeed job (retry: false), killing the entire feed poll. One stale topic_embed row (post deleted, e.g. by a moderator purge) makes every hourly PollFeed run raise on that item; with retry disabled the rest of the feed's new articles are never imported until someone manually deletes the row, and no error surfaces outside sidekiq's dead-job log.

[ADVISORY] fetch_http silently returns nil when embed_by_username is unset or the user was deleted, so the retrieve job reports success while doing no work and the embedded page never gets its topic. An admin who removes the embed_by_username user (or a typo'd username) gets a functioning-looking embed iframe that reloads the loading screen indefinitely; the failure is invisible because the job completes normally with no log line.

[ADVISORY] import_remote calls open(url) with no timeout and no read-size cap, so a slow or huge remote page hangs the Sidekiq worker indefinitely or loads an unbounded document into memory. A hung source server stalls the RetrieveTopic worker for the default Net::HTTP timeout (60s per socket read, unbounded overall), and an attacker or misconfigured feed page of arbitrary size is fully read into a string before readability parsing; workers exhaust and the embed loading loop times out client-side with no error surfaced.

[ADVISORY] poll_feed calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no timeout and no size limit, and SimpleRSS.parse on the raw body has no read cap, so a slow or enormous feed blocks the scheduled job and floods memory. A stalled feed server hangs the hourly PollFeed job with no timeout, and because TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute synchronously, that same unbounded fetch also blocks the interactive RetrieveTopic worker spawned by a visitor's embed request.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve runs the full PollFeed job synchronously inline in the RetrieveTopic worker whenever feed polling is enabled, so a visitor hitting an un-embedded page triggers a whole-feed import on the request-driven worker with no per-URL throttle on the poll itself. Each new embed_url view enqueues a RetrieveTopic that re-parses and re-imports the entire RSS feed inline (TopicEmbed.import is only deduped per-URL, not per-run), multiplying feed fetches by the number of distinct embed URLs first viewed in a poll interval — one slow feed server serializes these workers.

[ADVISORY] The loading view reloads unconditionally every 30 seconds with no failure counter or terminal error state, so any retrieval failure produces an endless reload loop instead of an error. End users on the embedding site see a permanently spinning 'Loading Discussion...' panel whenever the retrieve job fails or the throttle (60s redis key) keeps rejecting re-enqueues; there is no path from loading to an error or empty state, and the failure is invisible to both the visitor and the site operator.

[ADVISORY] The 'best' action enqueues RetrieveTopic fire-and-forget and renders loading with no feedback channel, so a job that fails permanently (network error fetching the article, readability parse failure) is never retried from the browser side because the redis throttle key marks the URL as retrieved before perform_retrieve's fetch actually succeeds. TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently sets retrieved:<url> via setnx with a 60s expiry before perform_retrieve runs; if the subsequent fetch raises, sidekiq's retry re-runs retrieve only while the throttle key lives — after 60 seconds the job's retries are all no-ops, and the embed page reloads forever against a URL that will never be fetched again in that window, reporting success (200 + loading page) while the work was dropped.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
