adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The raw_html cook_method returns raw completely outside the cooking pipeline — it bypasses both the Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook) hook and any sanitization that the normal cook path performs. Every plugin hooking after_post_cook (polls, oneboxes, math, etc.) silently no-ops for imported posts, and arbitrary HTML fetched from an external feed (attacker-controllable content in the feed) is stored verbatim as post.cooked and rendered with `raw` in the embed view — a stored-XSS ingestion path that the normal pipeline exists to prevent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking path (`post_analyzer.cook`) and also bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` entirely. `TopicEmbed.import` explicitly creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using `contents` sourced from RSS/Readability (`PollFeed` uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`; `import_remote` uses `doc.content`), and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. From the diff alone there is no sanitization step for this raw HTML path, so attacker-controlled feed/article HTML can be stored/rendered verbatim, creating a stored XSS ingestion path and also breaking expected plugin post-cook behavior for these posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key is defined (a SHA1 cache key for the feed's modified state) but never used anywhere — the poller re-downloads and re-parses the full feed unconditionally every hour. Dead code that documents an intent (conditional fetch / change detection) the implementation dropped; the next maintainer assumes feed modifications are checked and bandwidth is saved, when in fact every hour incurs a full fetch and full-iteration import regardless of feed changes.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, a `feed_key` method is introduced (`"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"`) but it is never referenced anywhere in the diff. The `poll_feed` method unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items` every time it runs, with no conditional fetch / change detection. This is real dead code and can mislead maintainers about intended caching/modified-state behavior, but it doesn’t constitute a functional correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten Disqus import drops both the created_at option (posts previously got Date.parse(t[:created_at])) and the category option, and now routes through TopicEmbed.import_remote which sets cook_method raw_html. Anyone re-running the disqus import after this change gets topics dated 'now' instead of their original thread dates (destroying chronological ordering of imported discussions) and can no longer target a category, plus imported content is now unsanitized raw HTML; the old CLI contract (--category flag) silently disappears.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes Disqus import behavior: `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` removes the `--category` option and no longer passes `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` into `PostCreator` (it now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `TopicEmbed.import` uses `PostCreator.new(... skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking pipeline. This means re-imports will create topics/posts with default timestamps ("now"), the category targeting CLI flag disappears, and imported HTML is rendered as-is via `raw_html`/`raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, which is a concrete behavioral/security regression relative to the previous importer contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] poll_feed calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no size limit, and import_remote calls open(url).read the same way, materializing the whole document in memory. A misconfigured or hostile feed_polling_url (or embeddable-host page, since embed URLs are attacker-supplied via the embed_url param and only host-checked) serving a multi-gigabyte response is read fully into the Sidekiq worker's memory, exhausting worker RAM for all tenants of that process.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces unbounded HTTP reads in background jobs: `Jobs::PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Neither enforces a maximum response size or streaming limit, so a very large feed/page response can be fully materialized in the Sidekiq worker’s memory, causing RAM exhaustion/DoS. `embed_url` is attacker-influenced via `EmbedController#best` → enqueue `:retrieve_topic`, and `TopicRetriever` only checks the host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, not size, so the risk is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] cook returns raw HTML unfiltered, bypassing the entire Markdown/sanitization pipeline including Plugin::Filter(:after_post_cook) for raw_html posts. RSS feed items and readability-extracted remote HTML fetched via feed_polling_url or import_remote are stored and served verbatim with raw post.cooked in embed/best and the main topic renderer, so a feed author or compromised embedded site injects arbitrary <script> into the Discourse origin — cookie/session theft on every visitor of the embedding host and the forum itself.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a raw-HTML bypass: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` immediately when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, skipping the normal cooking/sanitization and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` path. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true`, feeding in `contents` sourced from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no sanitization) and from remote pages (`import_remote` uses readability extraction, but still produces HTML). These posts are then rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `embed/best.html.erb`, and the cooked content would also be used when viewing the topic normally. This makes HTML/script injection plausible from a malicious feed item or compromised remote source.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] This diff adds force: true to create_table :top_topics on an already-shipped migration, so any environment that already ran the original version re-runs it and force-drops the existing top_topics table. Deploying this on a live site that has already executed the 20131223171005 migration destroys all top_topics rows (hot/daily/weekly/monthly top rankings) with no recovery path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which would drop/recreate the table *if that migration is executed*. However, Rails migrations do not automatically re-run on deploy in environments where `20131223171005_create_top_topics` has already been applied (it’s tracked in `schema_migrations`), so the claim that deploying this will “re-run it and force-drop the existing top_topics table” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] create_table :topic_embeds, force: true drops any pre-existing topic_embeds table instead of failing loudly. If topic_embeds was created out-of-band or by a prior deploy branch, running db:migrate silently discards all embed-to-topic mappings, orphaning imported topics and causing embed/best to re-import duplicate topics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` in `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`. In Rails migrations, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it, which can silently delete existing `topic_embeds` rows. If `topic_embeds` existed from an out-of-band/manual creation or another branch/deploy, running this migration would discard embed mappings as the finding describes, potentially leading to re-import/duplication behavior elsewhere in the diff (e.g., `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError when the feed item has no content element (common in Atom feeds where only summary is present). The hourly PollFeed job crashes on the first content-less item, retries are disabled (sidekiq_options retry: false), and every subsequent feed item is silently never imported — feed polling stops working with no operator-visible error beyond sidekiq dead-set noise.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (e.g., Atom entries that only have `summary`), `i.content` can be `nil`, making `nil.scrub` raise `NoMethodError`. There is no rescue/skip logic, so the job would abort mid-iteration, and `sidekiq_options retry: false` means Sidekiq will not retry that failed run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Disqus import rewrite silently changes accepted behavior: it drops the --category/-c option, discards the original thread created_at (posts now get import time instead of Date.parse(t[:created_at])), and no longer posts the [Permalink] raw — instead it fetches each thread over HTTP through readability. Operators running the documented disqus import after this change get topics in the default category with wrong timestamps and import failures whenever t[:link] is unreachable (TopicEmbed.import_remote does open(url)), breaking the previously-working offline import path with no deprecation notice.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` explicitly removes the `--category/-c` option and the logic that looked up `category_id`, and replaces the `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id, raw: "[Permalink](...)" )` path with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs `open(url).read` (network dependency) and ultimately creates posts via `PostCreator` without passing `created_at` or `category`, so imported topics will use default category and current timestamps, and imports can now fail if the remote URL is unreachable—behavioral breakage introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import mutates the caller's contents string with << and interpolates the raw URL into an HTML attribute, then wraps it in content_sha1, so the same RSS content with a URL containing a quote would both break the imported_from link markup and change the hash on every poll. Feed items whose link contains characters needing HTML escaping produce malformed imported posts; downstream, feed polls see a stable sha so updates stop being detected.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `contents << "\n<hr>...<a href='#{url}'>..."` both (1) mutates the caller-provided `contents` string in-place and (2) interpolates `url` directly into an HTML attribute without escaping. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and later rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `embed/best.html.erb`, a URL containing a single quote (or other HTML-breaking characters) would produce malformed HTML and could enable HTML injection. The in-place mutation is also an unexpected side effect that can alter the computed `content_sha1` if the same string object is reused across calls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] perform_retrieve runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside the RetrieveTopic background job rather than enqueuing it, performing a blocking HTTP fetch of the entire feed inside the retrieve path. Every embed miss from a non-staff visitor on a site with feed_polling_enabled triggers a full synchronous feed parse + per-item TopicEmbed.import inside a Sidekiq worker, making embed first-views arbitrarily slow and allowing the embeddable host's feed latency to consume worker capacity.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and parses/imports all items (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), so this can block the RetrieveTopic Sidekiq worker (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) during embed-miss handling. This is an architecture/performance concern grounded in the code, not a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When topic_id is found, TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) raises for a deleted/trashed topic and the view template dereferences @topic_view.topic.url on line 2 of best.html.erb without any posts-present guard on the header, so the loading-view branch's nil-safety is asymmetric with the found branch. A visitor embedding a URL whose topic was later deleted gets a 500 from /embed/best instead of a graceful fallback or the loading view.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows EmbedController#best blindly instantiates `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns an id, and `best.html.erb` unconditionally calls `@topic_view.topic.url` in the header (both branches) when that template is rendered. However, the claim that `TopicView.new` “raises for a deleted/trashed topic” is not verifiable from this diff because `TopicView` implementation and how deletions are represented are not shown. What is verifiable is an unhandled edge case: `topic_id_for_embed` can return an id even if the underlying topic/post is missing, and there is no rescue/fallback to `loading` or a graceful 404 in that path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The resize postMessage is sent to '<%= request.referer %>' as a literal targetOrigin while the receiving embed.js checks discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 with a leading-string prefix match. Any origin whose domain begins with the Discourse URL string (e.g. discourseUrl.example.attacker.com when discourseUrl is 'discourseUrl') passes the client check, and the iframe resizes on spoofed messages; combined with the raw-HTML rendering this is a second injection surface for the embedding page.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags that using `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` (an indexOf-based origin validation) is insufficient and can be bypassed by attacker-controlled origins crafted to appear as a prefix/similar string, allowing malicious domains to pass the check—matching the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] PollFeed imports unescaped RSS/Atom item content as a raw_html post with no HTML sanitization, which is then rendered verbatim. Unlike TopicEmbed.import_remote (which filters through Readability's tag/attribute whitelist), the poll_feed path calls TopicEmbed.import directly with CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) — so a malicious or compromised feed served at the admin-configured feed_polling_url injects arbitrary HTML (

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `raw_html` cook method where `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and stores `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` with `skip_validations: true` and no sanitization (app/models/topic_embed.rb). `Jobs::PollFeed` parses a remote feed and passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly into `TopicEmbed.import` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). This means arbitrary HTML from the feed is stored and rendered verbatim (e.g., embed view uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`), enabling stored XSS if the feed content is malicious/compromised. In contrast, `import_remote` applies a Readability tag/attribute whitelist, highlighting the missing sanitization in the feed path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import string-interpolates the URL into an HTML attribute without escaping, so a URL containing a single quote breaks out of the href attribute. A URL like http://embeddablehost/x' onmouseover='alert(1) passes the /^https?:\/\// regex check and embeddable_host match (host is unaffected by path characters) but injects arbitrary attributes/HTML into the 'imported_from' footer, which is stored as a raw_html post and rendered with `raw post.cooked`. An attacker who controls a page URL (e.g. a comment URL harvested by the RSS feed, or an embed_url path on the embeddable host) achieves stored XSS against all forum users.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an HTML footer that interpolates `url` directly into a single-quoted `href` attribute: `"#{url}"` (no escaping). The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or attribute-breaking characters in the path/query. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, this enables stored HTML/attribute injection (XSS) if an attacker can get a crafted URL into `TopicEmbed.import` (e.g., via RSS `i.link`/`i.id` or `embed_url`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embeddable-host gate is enforced by the client-controlled Referer header, making it trivially bypassable trust-the-client authorization. Anyone can curl /embed/best with a spoofed Referer matching embeddable_host and enumerate/render any topic's content via the TopicView branch (topic_id_for_embed performs no referer-independent scoping). The actual SSRF protection of the retriever does not depend on this check, so impact is limited to unauthorized content disclosure/crawling of a forum intended to be restricted to embedding on one host — but the gate provides no real boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` gate relies on `request.referer` (the client-supplied `Referer` header) to enforce `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`). Because clients can trivially spoof `Referer`, an attacker can `GET /embed/best?embed_url=...` with a forged header and pass the check. Once passed, the controller renders `TopicView` purely based on `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` with no additional, referer-independent scoping/authorization in this diff. This makes the “embeddable host” restriction ineffective and enables unauthorized access to the embed rendering endpoint (at least for any topic viewable as `current_user` nil).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of strict origin equality. Any origin whose string representation appears anywhere in discourseUrl passes the check; because origins are full scheme+host strings this is hard to exploit with the current constant, but it is a fragile pattern that silently breaks if discourseUrl ever contains a user-influenced component or redirects are followed. A future maintainer copying this pattern into a handler that mutates the DOM beyond iframe.height gets script injection on the embedding page.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is substring containment rather than strict origin equality. This is a real, diff-grounded robustness/security concern because it can accept unintended origins if `discourseUrl` ever contains additional components (e.g., path/query or unexpected concatenation), but the diff does not show `discourseUrl` being user-controlled nor does the handler currently do anything beyond setting `iframe.height`, so a concrete exploit/defect cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] request.referer is echoed directly into an inline <script> as a JS string literal. The Referer header is attacker-controlled and includes arbitrary path/query data; ERB's HTML escaping of quotes (to ') prevents JS execution but produces a malformed string / syntax error when the referer contains a single quote, breaking the resize postMessage for those embeds. Any string header interpolated into a script context should be JSON-encoded, not HTML-escaped.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, the inline script does `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>');`. `request.referer` comes from the Referer header (attacker-controlled) and is inserted into a JavaScript string context using Rails’ default HTML escaping, not JS/JSON encoding. This is diff-verifiable. While HTML escaping typically prevents breaking out of the quoted JS string (so the finding’s specific “syntax error on single quote” claim is overstated), it can still break functionality because the `targetOrigin` argument should be an origin (scheme+host+port) and not an arbitrary full URL/path/query or HTML-entity–mangled string, causing `postMessage` to be rejected/throw and the resize messaging to fail. Proper fix would be to derive an origin and JSON-encode it (e.g., `URI(request.referer).origin.to_json`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) uses Kernel#open on a configuration value, which executes shell commands when the value begins with a pipe character. Ruby's open() treats a string starting with '|' as a command to run, so any actor able to set site settings (or compromise the settings store) gets arbitrary command execution on the app server rather than just an HTTP fetch. Per the config-as-attacker-input threat model, config-backed sinks into open() should be treated as command-injection-capable; use open-uri's URI(...) or Net::HTTP instead.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the diff adds `require 'open-uri'` and then calls `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. This uses `open(...)` on a site setting value without wrapping/validating it as a URI. In Ruby, `Kernel#open` (and `open-uri`’s extension of it) treats strings beginning with `|` as a command to execute, so a malicious `feed_polling_url` setting could trigger command execution rather than an HTTP fetch. This is a concrete security defect grounded in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] import_remote calls open(url) with the user-supplied embed_url, and open() invokes command execution for pipe-prefixed strings. The invalid_host? check (URI(@embed_url).host == embeddable_host) rejects pipe-prefixed strings since URI() raises, so this path is currently contained; but the safety depends on TopicRetriever always running before import_remote — the Disqus thor task calls import_remote directly with t[:link] from a local file, so any future caller that skips the retriever check gets command execution from unvalidated input. The command-injection primitive (Kernel#open on untrusted URLs) should be removed, not merely gated upstream.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `open(url).read` on its `url` argument (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The diff also introduces at least one `require 'open-uri'` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), which enables the `Kernel#open` behavior where pipe-prefixed strings can invoke command execution. `import_remote` itself performs no scheme/host validation, and the Disqus thor task now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` directly (lib/tasks/disqus.thor), bypassing the `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` gate entirely. This makes the safety dependent on upstream callers and leaves a command-execution primitive reachable from unvalidated input within the codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The test named "is 404 without an embed_url" asserts only response.should_not be_success, and the params.require branch is never reached because ensure_embeddable raises first when embeddable_host is unset. The test passes whether the controller returns a 404, a 403, or a 500, and the params.require(:embed_url) path has zero test coverage — a regression that breaks the missing-param contract (e.g., raising a 500 instead of 400) would go undetected because the error thrown by the before_filter masks it.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController`, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before `best`. `ensure_embeddable` raises if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` or if `request.referer` host doesn’t match. The spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do get :best` sets neither `embeddable_host` nor a referer, so the request will fail in the before_filter and never reach `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` in `best`. The assertion `response.should_not be_success` would pass for any non-2xx (403/404/500), so the missing-`embed_url` path and its specific contract aren’t actually covered by this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'tells the topic retriever to work' test verifies only that a TopicRetriever mock's retrieve method is called, never that Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) receives the correct embed_url and user_id payload that the controller actually constructs. The argument-passing from controller to job to retriever (embed_url string, user_id for current_user) is unverified; if Jobs.enqueue is a no-op in test mode the expectation goes unfulfilled or the inline path silently skips user_id, and a regression dropping or mangling the embed_url in the enqueue payload would not be caught.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the controller enqueues a job with `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` when no topic is found. The spec `"tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found"` does not assert anything about `Jobs.enqueue` being called or about the payload (`embed_url`, `user_id`) passed into the job; it only expects `TopicRetriever.new`/`retrieve` to happen (presumably via whatever `Jobs.enqueue` does in test mode). That leaves the controller→job argument contract untested and could miss regressions in the enqueued arguments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'creates a topic view' test fully mocks TopicView.new, so the best.html.erb view — including the new @topic_view.posts.present? branches and raw post.cooked rendering — is never rendered or asserted. Any breakage in the new embed view template (nil post.user, wrong posts collection from the best:5 option) passes the controller spec; only the mocked constructor call is verified, testing the mock rather than the rendered behavior the diff adds.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the "creates a topic view when a topic_id is found" example fully stubs/expects `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` and the controller spec does not enable `render_views`, so the new `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` template (including `@topic_view.posts.present?` branching and `raw post.cooked` rendering) is not exercised. This means breakage in the new embed view/template behavior could pass while only the constructor call is verified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every test in poll_feed_spec only exercises the settings gate in execute (poll_feed never/once) — the actual poll_feed method (SimpleRSS parsing, the url-blank/non-http fallback to i.id, CGI.unescapeHTML with scrub, delegation to TopicEmbed.import) has zero assertions anywhere in the diff. The feed-import logic — including the branch where i.link is blank or non-http and falls back to i.id — can regress entirely while all four specs stay green; an operator enabling feed polling gets untested code parsing arbitrary remote feeds.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` contains nontrivial new feed-import logic (e.g., `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, `url = i.link` with fallback to `i.id` when blank or non-HTTP, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import(...)`). However, `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests `execute`’s settings gate by asserting `poll_feed` is called or not called; it never exercises or asserts any behavior of `poll_feed` itself. No other added/modified specs in the diff cover these branches, so the core feed parsing/import behavior could regress while the current specs remain green.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] All 'valid host' tests stub retrieved_recently?, so the real Redis throttle (setnx + 60s expire in retrieved_recent?), perform_retrieve's early return on existing TopicEmbed, the PollFeed delegation, and fetch_http are never executed by any test. A bug in the Redis throttle logic (e.g., key never set, or expire missing so throttling becomes permanent) or in perform_retrieve's exist-check ordering passes the suite untouched; only the boolean gate dispatch is covered.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the “valid host” examples stub TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? to return true/false and only assert dispatch to perform_retrieve (or not). This means the real Redis throttling logic in retrieved_recently? ($redis.setnx + expire 60) is never exercised by tests. Additionally, no test in the diff executes perform_retrieve itself, so its early return on TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?, its optional Jobs::PollFeed invocation, and the fetch_http -> TopicEmbed.import_remote path are not covered. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls is only tested with a default-port http URL; the non-standard-port branch (prefix << ":#{uri.port}") and TopicEmbed.import_remote (ruby-readability document parsing, tags/attributes whitelist, opts[:title] fallback) have no test in the diff. The port-appending branch can produce malformed URLs (double slashes, wrong scheme) without detection, and import_remote — the path used by the Disqus thor task and the retrieve_topic job — can break (Readability API change, open(url) failure) with the entire spec suite green.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial logic in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (uses `ruby-readability` and `open(url).read`, applies tag/attribute whitelists, falls back to `opts[:title] || doc.title`) and in `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` includes a distinct branch to append non-default ports (`prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`). The added specs (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) only exercise an `http` URL without an explicit port and do not cover `import_remote` at all. While the finding’s claim that the port-branch can produce malformed URLs is not demonstrated by the shown implementation, the lack of coverage for these new branches/paths is a concrete, diff-grounded review issue rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Jobs::RetrieveTopic has no spec anywhere in the diff (checked spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb — none reference RetrieveTopic), so the user lookup, the raise on missing embed_url, and the no_throttle: user.try(:staff?) option are untested. A regression in the job (e.g., enqueuing with a stale user_id causing user to be nil and throttling staff incorrectly, or the InvalidParameters raise firing on every call) surfaces only in production sidekiq, not in CI.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new Sidekiq job `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` (including logic to raise on missing `args[:embed_url]`, look up `User` by `args[:user_id]`, and pass `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` into `TopicRetriever`). The diff also starts enqueuing it from `EmbedController#best` via `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)`. The added specs cover `TopicRetriever`, `EmbedController`, `PollFeed`, and `TopicEmbed`, but there is no spec file covering `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, so this new job’s behavior is untested in CI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] An already-shipped migration was retroactively modified to add force: true, making it destructive on re-run. Running db:migrate:redo or db:rollback past this version on a production database executes DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics and silently destroys all top_topics rows (daily/weekly/monthly score aggregates) with no backup/export step; the data is unrecoverable without recomputation, and the change ships in a PR whose feature (topic embeds) has nothing to do with top_topics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does retroactively change an existing migration: `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` now uses `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which (in Rails) will drop the table if it already exists. However, for databases that have already run this migration, the edited file will not be re-executed during normal `db:migrate`, so it doesn’t introduce an immediate, verifiable defect for typical production upgrades. The reviewer’s specific claim about `db:migrate:redo`/rolling back causing data loss is not uniquely caused by this change (rolling back/redoing a `create_table` migration already drops the table). Still, modifying a shipped migration and adding `force: true` increases risk in scenarios where migrations are re-run or the schema_migrations state is inconsistent, making it a concrete, diff-grounded concern but not a clear new bug in standard flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new topic_embeds migration uses force: true on a table that, once shipped and populated, will be dropped and its data lost if the migration is ever re-run (redo, or a fresh db:migrate against an environment where the table pre-exists from a prior deploy). After this migration ships and TopicEmbed rows accumulate, any db:migrate:redo or rollback+re-run wipes every topic_embed mapping; embedded sites then re-import articles as duplicate topics because embed_url lookups find nothing, silently forking comment threads off existing posts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` with `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists and recreates it, which would delete any accumulated `topic_embeds` data if the migration is re-run (e.g., `db:migrate:redo` or applied in an environment where the table already exists). Since `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` relies on persisted rows (`where(embed_url: ...)`), losing them can cause re-import/duplication as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] topic_id and post_id are created null: false with no foreign key constraints and no indexes, while TopicEmbed#import updates the associated post on every content change and embed_controller reads topic_id from this table. Deleting a topic or post (standard Discourse behavior, e.g. after post destroy jobs) leaves orphaned topic_embeds rows; TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed then returns a topic_id for a nonexistent topic and EmbedController#best constructs TopicView.new with a deleted topic id, erroring on the embed endpoint — and without an index on topic_id, the periodic import re-lookups degrade. Orphan cleanup has to be handled out-of-band forever because the migration never establishes referential integrity.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` declared `null: false` but only indexes `embed_url` (no FK constraints, no index on `topic_id`/`post_id`): `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`. `EmbedController#best` trusts `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and then calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` without verifying the topic exists. Since nothing in this diff enforces cascading cleanup of `topic_embeds` when a `Topic` or `Post` is deleted, orphan rows are possible and could later cause the embed endpoint to look up a non-existent topic id. However, claims about import lookup performance degrading due to missing `topic_id` index aren’t well supported by the shown queries (most lookups are by `embed_url`, which is indexed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The update path revises the embed's post but writes only the new raw via PostRevisor with skip_validations, and if post is nil (the embed row exists but its post_id points at a deleted post, allowed by the missing FK above), PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises and the PollFeed job dies, blocking all subsequent feed items from importing. A single stale topic_embed row (topic/post deleted by a moderator while the RSS feed still lists the article) makes the hourly PollFeed job raise before reaching remaining feed items — with retry: false set on the job, every poll after that silently fails and the feed stops importing until the orphan row is manually removed.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path assumes `embed.post` exists: it assigns `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally does `PostRevisor.new(post)` when the SHA changes. The migration `create_topic_embeds` adds `post_id`/`topic_id` integers but no foreign keys, so an orphaned `topic_embeds` row (e.g., post deleted) can leave `embed.post == nil`, causing `PostRevisor` to later blow up when it uses `@post`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` iterates items with no rescue, so such an exception would abort the job mid-loop, preventing subsequent feed items from importing in that run; `sidekiq_options retry: false` further reduces recovery.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new NOT NULL cook_method column relies on its integer default to backfill every existing post, coupling the existing-row semantics to the Post.cook_methods Enum ordering rather than a named constant or comment, with no migration-side assertion of what 1 means. Future maintainers reordering or inserting values into Post.cook_methods (e.g. adding a :markdown method first) silently reclassify the backfilled rows: all existing posts render through the wrong cook pipeline after a code change with no migration accompanying it. The value is correct today (1 = :regular) but the coupling is undocumented at the migration site.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `posts.cook_method` via migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` while the meaning of `1` is implicitly defined by `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. The migration itself contains no comment/assertion tying `1` to `:regular`, so future reordering/insertion into `cook_methods` could change what `1` represents without a corresponding migration, affecting how existing rows are interpreted. This is a maintainability/migration-robustness issue rather than an immediate defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import returns nil silently when PostCreator.create fails, and the RetrieveTopic job then completes 'successfully' with no topic created, so the embed iframe loops on the loading page forever. The embed controller renders 'loading' and reloads every 30s (loading.html.erb); if the article fetch fails or the post is rejected (e.g., empty title/content after readability extraction), the job enqueued from EmbedController#best completes with no error, no embed row is created, and the visitor's browser reloads /embed/best in an infinite loop with no error ever surfaced to the user or the logs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a silent failure path that can leave the embed page permanently in the `loading` reload loop. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when creating a new embed, it calls `PostCreator.new(...).create` and only creates the `TopicEmbed` row if `post.present?`; if `create` returns nil/blank, the method just returns nil and does not create an embed row or raise/log anything (app/models/topic_embed.rb). In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), and `loading.html.erb` reloads the page every 30s. `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever` also do not check for or surface a failed import; they just call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb, lib/topic_retriever.rb). Therefore, if import consistently fails without raising (e.g., `PostCreator#create` returns nil), the embed never appears and the browser reloads indefinitely with no error surfaced, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] A single bad feed item aborts the whole items loop with an unhandled NoMethodError (i.content or i.title nil for a valid Atom entry), and with sidekiq_options retry: false the remaining items are permanently dropped with no retry. The first item missing content raises NoMethodError on i.content.scrub; every subsequent item in the feed is skipped, and because retry is disabled there is no later attempt — feed items are silently missing from the forum with no log identifying which item broke the run.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` with no nil-guards or per-item rescue. If a feed item lacks `content` (valid for some Atom/RSS variants), `i.content` can be nil and `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire `rss.items.each` run and preventing processing of later items. The job also sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so failures won’t be retried by Sidekiq, increasing the chance items are missed if the feed doesn’t continue to include older entries on the next hourly run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On the update path, embed.post is dereferenced without a nil check, so an embed row whose post was deleted crashes with NoMethodError inside the scheduled PollFeed job (retry: false), killing the entire feed poll. One stale topic_embed row (post deleted, e.g. by a moderator purge) makes every hourly PollFeed run raise on that item; with retry disabled the rest of the feed's new articles are never imported until someone manually deletes the row, and no error surfaces outside sidekiq's dead-job log.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally uses it (`PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revisor.revise!`) when the content hash changes. If the associated post has been deleted, `embed.post` will be `nil`, leading to an exception (likely `NoMethodError` inside `PostRevisor`). `Jobs::PollFeed` iterates `rss.items.each` without rescue and has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single stale `topic_embeds` row can abort the entire poll run and prevent later items from importing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] fetch_http silently returns nil when embed_by_username is unset or the user was deleted, so the retrieve job reports success while doing no work and the embedded page never gets its topic. An admin who removes the embed_by_username user (or a typo'd username) gets a functioning-looking embed iframe that reloads the loading screen indefinitely; the failure is invisible because the job completes normally with no log line.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, the code looks up the configured user and then `return if user.blank?` with no error/log: `user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first; return if user.blank?` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). When this happens, the retrieve path does no work and no `TopicEmbed` is created, so `EmbedController#best` will keep rendering `loading` (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb reloads every 30s) because `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` continues to return nil. The finding’s “unset embed_by_username” part is slightly off (nil would raise on `.downcase`), but the “typo’d username / deleted user causes silent no-op and endless loading” is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] import_remote calls open(url) with no timeout and no read-size cap, so a slow or huge remote page hangs the Sidekiq worker indefinitely or loads an unbounded document into memory. A hung source server stalls the RetrieveTopic worker for the default Net::HTTP timeout (60s per socket read, unbounded overall), and an attacker or misconfigured feed page of arbitrary size is fully read into a string before readability parsing; workers exhaust and the embed loading loop times out client-side with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces unbounded remote fetches in background jobs: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) with no timeout options and reads the entire response into a single String before parsing, and `Jobs::PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) similarly. This can hang Sidekiq workers on slow/unresponsive servers and/or exhaust memory on very large responses. The risk is directly introduced by these new code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] poll_feed calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no timeout and no size limit, and SimpleRSS.parse on the raw body has no read cap, so a slow or enormous feed blocks the scheduled job and floods memory. A stalled feed server hangs the hourly PollFeed job with no timeout, and because TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute synchronously, that same unbounded fetch also blocks the interactive RetrieveTopic worker spawned by a visitor's embed request.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, PollFeed#poll_feed does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (via open-uri) with no explicit timeout or maximum read size, so a slow/stalled server can block the Sidekiq worker and an extremely large response can consume excessive memory. This is made worse by lib/topic_retriever.rb where TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when feed polling is enabled, meaning the same unbounded network fetch can also block the interactive embed-driven RetrieveTopic flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] perform_retrieve runs the full PollFeed job synchronously inline in the RetrieveTopic worker whenever feed polling is enabled, so a visitor hitting an un-embedded page triggers a whole-feed import on the request-driven worker with no per-URL throttle on the poll itself. Each new embed_url view enqueues a RetrieveTopic that re-parses and re-imports the entire RSS feed inline (TopicEmbed.import is only deduped per-URL, not per-run), multiplying feed fetches by the number of distinct embed URLs first viewed in a poll interval — one slow feed server serializes these workers.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (not enqueued) before falling back to HTTP fetch. `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` on first view of a new `embed_url`, and `TopicRetriever` throttles only per-`embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so distinct embed URLs can each trigger a full feed fetch/parse via `PollFeed#poll_feed` (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) with no feed-level throttling/caching. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff, though not a strict correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading view reloads unconditionally every 30 seconds with no failure counter or terminal error state, so any retrieval failure produces an endless reload loop instead of an error. End users on the embedding site see a permanently spinning 'Loading Discussion...' panel whenever the retrieve job fails or the throttle (60s redis key) keeps rejecting re-enqueues; there is no path from loading to an error or empty state, and the failure is invisible to both the visitor and the site operator.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the page unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds with no max retries or error state. In `EmbedController#best`, when no embed exists it always enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders this loading template. If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., network/open-uri failure in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, invalid/missing `embed_by_username`, or `TopicRetriever` throttling/host rejection), the user-facing embed will remain in a perpetual reload loop with no terminal error/empty UI. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/operability gap but not a directly provable functional crash/incorrectness within the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'best' action enqueues RetrieveTopic fire-and-forget and renders loading with no feedback channel, so a job that fails permanently (network error fetching the article, readability parse failure) is never retried from the browser side because the redis throttle key marks the URL as retrieved before perform_retrieve's fetch actually succeeds. TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently sets retrieved:<url> via setnx with a 60s expiry before perform_retrieve runs; if the subsequent fetch raises, sidekiq's retry re-runs retrieve only while the throttle key lives — after 60 seconds the job's retries are all no-ops, and the embed page reloads forever against a URL that will never be fetched again in that window, reporting success (200 + loading page) while the work was dropped.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? the Redis throttle key ("retrieved:#{@embed_url}") is set via setnx/expire *before* perform_retrieve runs. If perform_retrieve (e.g. TopicEmbed.import_remote -> open(url).read / Readability::Document.new) raises, Sidekiq will retry the job, but the next retry within 60s will hit retrieved_recently? == true and return without doing any fetch, and without raising—effectively marking the retry as a success and stopping further Sidekiq retries. This can cause failed retrieves to be dropped/delayed until some external trigger (like the embed page reloading after the throttle expires) enqueues a new job.
